'''''Allium neapolitanum''''' is a bulbous [[herbaceous]] perennial plant in the [[Allioideae|onion subfamily]] within the [[Amaryllis family]]. Common names include '''Neapolitan garlic''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''Naples garlic''', '''daffodil garlic''', '''false garlic''', '''flowering onion''', '''Naples onion''', '''Guernsey star-of-Bethlehem''', '''star''', '''white garlic''', and '''wood garlic'''.

== Description ==
''Allium neapolitanum'' produces round [[bulb]]s up to {{convert|2|cm|abbr=on|frac=4}} across. The [[scape (botany)|scape]] is  up to {{convert|25|cm|in|abbr=on|frac=2}} tall, round in cross-section but sometimes with wings toward the bottom. The inflorescence is an [[umbel]] of up to 25 white flowers with yellow [[anthers]].<ref name="AF">{{Cite web |title=Allium flower, ''Allium neapolitanum'' |url=http://www.alliumflower.net/allium_neapolitanum/allium_neapolitanum.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100329145237/http://www.alliumflower.net/allium_neapolitanum/allium_neapolitanum.html |archive-date=2010-03-29 |access-date=2010-03-04}}</ref><ref name="sdfwert2495245">[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242101377 Flora of North America v 26 p 257 ''Allium neapolitanum'']</ref><ref>Cirillo, Domenico Maria Leone. 1788. Plantarum Rariorum Regni Neapolitani 1: 13.</ref><ref>[http://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/get_JM_treatment.pl?8349,8354,8396 Hickman, J. C. 1993. The Jepson Manual: Higher Plants of California 1–1400. University of California Press, Berkeley. ]</ref>

''Allium neapolitanum'' seems to have [[beta-adrenergic antagonist]] properties.<ref>{{cite journal|vauthors =Nencini C, Franchi GG, Micheli L|date=June 2010|journal=International Journal of Food Sciences and Nutrition|volume=61|issue=4|pages=433–9|title=Cardiovascular receptor binding affinity of aqueous extracts from Allium species|pmid=20446820|doi=10.3109/09637481003591608|s2cid=41881100}}</ref>

== Distribution and habitat ==
Its native range extends across the [[Mediterranean Region]] from [[Portugal]] to the [[Levant]].<ref>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do;jsessionid=6ACD213738988E637EEC4C4C809A078C?name_id=296083 Kew Botanical Gardens, World Checklist of Selected Plant Families, Allium neapolitanum Cirillo]</ref><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=allium+neapolitanum Altervista Flora Italiana, ''Allium neapolitanum'']</ref> The species is cultivated as an ornamental and has become naturalized in many areas, including [[Pakistan]], [[Australia]], [[New Zealand]], and in southern and western parts of the United States. It is classed as an [[invasive species]] in parts of the U.S.,<ref>{{Cite PLANTS |symbol=ALNE3 |taxon=Allium neapolitanum |access-date= }}</ref> and is found primarily in the states of [[California]], [[Texas]], [[Louisiana]], and [[Florida]].<ref name="AF" /><ref name="sdfwert2495245" />
